reviewed_by: Claude review of in-band streaming error frames
reason: The OpenAI-compatible SSE loop in _stream_openai_compatible read only choices, usage and ids from each data frame. OpenRouter, vLLM and similar gateways report an upstream failure that happens after the 200 headers were sent as a {"error": {...}} data frame, so such a frame produced no events and the stream ended with a COMPLETED event carrying empty text: the operator saw an empty successful reply (or a truncated one) with no failure, and nothing retried or explained it. _stream_error_frame now maps that frame to ProviderError (ProviderContextLengthError for context-length codes and markers) using the same detail extraction as HTTP errors, factored into _error_detail and _context_length_error so both paths unwrap OpenRouter's metadata.raw upstream reason. Raising inside the stream body reaches the existing except that yields a StreamEventType.ERROR event with the message, which chat.py already turns into a failed turn; _stream_with_retry never replays a started stream, so no retry happens. test_providers covers the frame after partial output, the frame before any token, the typed context-length mapping, and all existing HTTP error, retry and streaming cases.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change; the failure renders through the existing turn error path. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (matched through the remaining-core fallback for providers.py) is the real-Core journey suite and cannot inject a provider error frame; the Python provider suite exercises the transport with httpx.MockTransport. No full suites.
